title: [Chapitre] VIII. Analysis situs (quatrième mouture) : notes manuscrites (26/06-04/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
This page sits inside Grothendieck's 1986 'Analysis situs' (fourth draft), where he builds a combinatorial or axiomatic theory of 'magasins' (also 'mégaris'). A magasin is a set of abstract figures (cells) carrying several relations:
- ≤, the face or sub-figure relation;
- ≪ (dotted <), interior inclusion;
- |∘|, disjointness ('étrangers');
- ‖, the analogous relation between a figure and a family of figures.
For a family F of figures he has an 'open support' supp°(F), the set of figures covered by F.

On the previous page he states the 'axiome des supports' (Axiom supp 1). Take a family F, a subfamily Φ ⊂ F, and the complement Φ' = F∖Φ. Then supp°(F) ∩ cosupp°(Φ) = supp°(Φ'). Equivalently: any figure Z lying in the support of F and disjoint from every member of Φ already lies in the support of the remaining figures Φ'. The axiom involves only ≤ and |∘| (or ‖), not ≪.

On this page he comments that this is the first axiom 'of delicate nature' he has met. It holds automatically when the magasin is 'fidèle', or more generally whenever there is a fully faithful set-theoretic (categorical) support function. Such a function realizes figures as subsets of a point set so that the relations become inclusion and disjointness. The axiom then reduces to the set-theoretic tautology: Z ⊂ A ∪ B and Z ∩ A = ∅ imply Z ⊂ B.

The first interesting case where such a realization is not obviously available is the magasin attached to an ordered set. He decides to introduce it formally and study it 'from the viewpoint of supports'. He sets a three-point programme:
1. Treat magasins defined by an ordered set. On the next page (1 July) this is done for a dense total order L: point-figures P_x = {{x}} and segment-figures S_{a,b} = {[a,b], {a}, {b}}, with ∂S_{a,b} = {P_a, P_b}, and ≤, ≪ and |∘| made explicit.
2. Treat magasins defined by ≤ and |∘| alone, with ≪ and the supports derived from them. A deleted passage tries to give meaning to x° = Supp°(x_1, …) and hence y° ⊂ x°.
3. Ask whether in these 'disjunctive' magasins there are obvious examples where the support axiom fails. A later marginal note on the asterisk answers 'Oui!': such counterexamples exist.

So the page is a methodological pivot. It isolates the one axiom that does not follow formally from the others, explains why set-theoretic models make it trivial, and plans to test it on order-theoretic and purely disjointness-defined models.
errors: No mathematical error. The claim that a fully faithful support function forces the axiom is correct, provided the realization reflects both the support/≤ relation and disjointness |∘| (it then reduces to Z ⊂ A∪B, Z∩A=∅ ⇒ Z ⊂ B). The marginal 'Oui!' records that the axiom genuinely fails in some 'disjunctive' magasins. This confirms it is independent of the ≤/|∘| structure alone, but no counterexample is written on this page.

ideas.what: The 'axiome des supports': a figure covered by a family F and disjoint from a subfamily Φ is covered by the complement F∖Φ. It is a cancellation or locality axiom for abstract covering by figures.
ideas.modern_name: Distributivity/cancellation law for covers; analogous to the 'disjointness/contact' axioms of Boolean contact algebras and mereotopology, and to separation properties of abstract cell complexes
ideas.usually_credited_to: Mereotopology: Whitehead, de Laguna, Clarke; contact algebras: Dimov–Vakarelov (2000s); abstract cell complexes: Steinitz, Tucker, Kovalevsky
ideas.where_published: Only in the unpublished Analysis situs manuscripts (Montpellier, cote 156)

ideas.what: Fully faithful 'support functions': realizations of an abstract magasin as subsets of a point set that reflect the order and disjointness relations. These make all set-theoretic axioms automatic.
ideas.modern_name: Representation theorems: Stone/Priestley-type representation, spatiality of locales or contact algebras; realization of face posets as regular CW complexes
ideas.usually_credited_to: Stone (1936); for contact algebras, Düntsch–Winter and Dimov–Vakarelov
ideas.where_published: unpublished; tame topology is announced only programmatically in Esquisse d'un programme (1984)

ideas.what: Magasins associated with ordered sets (dense total orders, points and segments) as the first test case where faithful realization is not automatic.
ideas.modern_name: Cell structure / face poset of an ordered line; o-minimal-type 1-dimensional cell decomposition
ideas.usually_credited_to: o-minimality: van den Dries, Pillay–Steinhorn, Knight (1980s)

ideas.what: 'Disjunctive' magasins defined only by ≤ and disjointness |∘|, with interior inclusion ≪ and supports derived from them.
ideas.modern_name: Part-of plus disjointness (contact) structures; region-based theories of space; the 'well-inside' relation derived from contact, as in proximity spaces and contact algebras

missed.claim: Grothendieck derives the interior relation ≪ from ≤ and disjointness |∘| alone, and tests a covering axiom that holds exactly when a set-theoretic representation exists. This is structurally the same problem treated in point-free topology and mereotopology: deriving 'well-inside' from contact (de Vries algebras, Boolean contact algebras) and asking when a region structure is representable by sets. The link between his Analysis situs/tame-topology program and mereotopology and contact algebras does not seem to have been made in the literature.
missed.quote: Examiner le cas des magasins définis par ≤, |∘| seulement (le ≪ étant défini via ≤, |∘| ...) ... Voir si dans ces magasins "disjonctifs", on n'aurait pas des exemples évidents où l'axiome des supports serait en défaut
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Representation theorems for contact algebras and their failure cases could supply exactly the counterexamples and representability criteria Grothendieck was seeking. Conversely, his cell-based axioms might give a combinatorial, finite-cell version of region-based topology.

missed.claim: Grothendieck records ('Oui!') that the support axiom fails in some disjunctive magasins. The page does not record the counterexample or the corrected axiom system; one would have to check the following pages (around pp. 97–98 cited on the next page). He also leaves open whether ordered-set magasins admit fully faithful support functions.
missed.quote: on n'aurait pas des exemples évidents où l'axiome des supports serait en défaut...* / * Oui!
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Characterizing which abstract cell or figure structures admit faithful set-theoretic realization is a live question for combinatorial models of tame topology and digital topology.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a planning page in an unpublished axiomatics. The content (independence of a covering axiom, testing it on order-theoretic models) is natural rather than striking. The mild interest is the unexplored parallel with mereotopology and contact algebras, and the unrecorded counterexample marked 'Oui!'.
transcription_corrections: 'C'est la première axiome' should read 'C'est le premier axiome de nature délicate'.
'(car alors y a une fonction support cat.' is more likely '(car on y a une fonction support cat.'.
In 2°, the relations are '≤, |∘| seulement (le ≪ étant défini via ≤, |∘|' — the defined relation is ≪, not ≤.
Struck passage: 'cette description... permettant de donner un sens à la relation x° = Supp°(X1 …), donc Y° ⊂ X° (en définissant ≪ ...)'; the next line is 'en définir en conséquence ≪'.
'Le premier cas intéressant rencontré où il n'est pas sûr qu'on ait une telle fonction support' — 'qu'on ait' rather than 'que l'on ait'.
Item 1°: 'regarder le cas des magasins [associés, struck] définis par un ens ordonné' — the struck word looks like 'associés' and is overwritten with 'définis par un'.
